name: TS5A63157DBVR
title: 12 Ω SPDT analog switch, 1.65 V to 5.5 V
summary: A single-pole double-throw analog switch, a 2:1 multiplexer or demultiplexer, running from one 1.65 V to 5.5 V supply. IN low joins COM to NC, IN high joins COM to NO, with break-before-make timing; signals from ground to V+ pass both ways. The I/O pins are guarded against overshoot and undershoot and go high impedance when V+ is 0 V, and the select input takes 5.5 V at any supply. Offered in 6-pin SOT-23 (DBV) and SC-70 (DCK), -40 °C to 85 °C.
key_figures: 4 Ω typ, 8 Ω max at V+ = 4.5 V, 25 °C
4.6 Ω typ at 4.5 V; 13.8 Ω typ at 1.65 V

circuits.title: System schematic
circuits.description: A controller picks which of two outside lines reaches one of its own pins. Its select output drives IN, held low by a resistor to ground so COM rests on NC until the controller drives IN high; its signal pin meets COM and the switch passes the signal either way to NO or NC. V+ comes from the 5 V rail with a decoupling capacitor to ground.

parts.note: decoupling on V+; 0.1 µF for a single-supply part
pull-down on IN; sized for the GPIO drive, power and switching rate

notes: The design requirements give V+ = 1.8 V for this example; any supply in the recommended range works.
With an open-drain GPIO, R1 becomes a pull-up.

where.VNO or VNC: voltage at the closed NO or NC terminal

where.QC: charge moved onto the output by a select edge, in coulombs

equations.name: Trace width at a square corner

where.Wcorner: width across the apex of a 90° bend

operation.text: One SPDT channel. IN low connects COM to NC; IN high connects COM to NO. Signals from 0 V up to V+ pass in both directions, analog or digital.
On a select change the closed path opens before the other closes, so NO and NC are never joined through COM. The gap is tBBM, 0.5 ns minimum.

Circuits at the I/O pins detect a signal pulled above V+ or below ground and keep an OFF switch from turning on while it lasts. Tested with a 20 ns pulse from -2 V to 5.5 V on an OFF channel's input, the output stays within 0.3 V of VOH during undershoot and of VOL during overshoot.
With V+ = 0 V the I/O pins go high impedance, so signals may be present before the supply comes up. NO/NC and COM leakage at V+ = 0 is in the tables as INC(PWROFF), INO(PWROFF) and ICOM(PWROFF).
IN accepts up to 5.5 V at any supply from 1.65 V to 5.5 V. Its thresholds are 0.7 × V+ and 0.3 × V+ from 3 V to 5.5 V, and 0.75 × V+ and 0.25 × V+ from 1.65 V to 2.7 V.

NO, NC or COM not in use may float or go to GND. IN must always sit high or low: at a threshold level its input transistors half conduct, raising supply current and leaving the switch state undefined.
A 0.1 µF bypass capacitor on V+, placed as close to the pin as possible. Bypass capacitors may be paralleled to reject noise at different frequencies; 0.1 µF with 1 µF is a common pair.

A square 90° trace corner is wider across its apex, changes its impedance and causes reflections. Two 45° bends, with the inner leg at least one trace width long, are better; a rounded bend of constant width is best.
Routing audio or video, sample-and-hold stages, communication links and battery-powered gear: wherever one line must be taken from one of two sources.
Latch-up immunity above 100 mA (JESD 78, class II). ESD 2000 V human-body model and 1000 V charged-device model.
